layers.note: Fire Effects Information System species review of Scouler's willow (Anderson 2001): a tall shrub or small tree; it forms a tall shrub layer in young stands and becomes a small tree at low to mid elevations.

moisture.note: Fire Effects Information System species review of Scouler's willow (Anderson 2001): found in drier habitats than most willows, on moderately to well-drained soils, most often on moist ground and intermittent watercourses, rarely on wet; its cover is greatest at intermediate soil moisture.

heat_load.note: Grows on any aspect, as Pacific willow's range is read.

elevation_m.note: Fire Effects Information System species review of Scouler's willow (Anderson 2001): from sea level to over 3,000 m.

max_slope_deg.note: Fire Effects Information System species review of Scouler's willow (Anderson 2001): level to moderately sloping ground, and steep dry slopes in the south-west; 35 degrees is this niche's reading.

shade_tolerance.note: Fire Effects Information System species review of Scouler's willow (Anderson 2001): a shade-intolerant, persistent seral species; it persists only under thin canopies, peaks in stands 30 to 40 years old and is gone from stands past 150 years.

coldest_c.note: Taken from Pacific willow's niche: both range from Alaska to California and the Rockies (FEIS); an approximate envelope.

moisture_index.note: Drier than Pacific willow, which the water's edge keeps wet: upland ground, gone in the driest climates (below about 0.1).
